description: We are trying our hands on this new challenge to explore new grounds and learn new things.
summary:
Week As A Marstronaut is a game about exploring Mars and managing an outpost. The game focuses on mission status and how to manage resources. Players go through the Mars environment. Move around the Outpost. They keep an eye on systems like health, radiation, hunger, battery and the health of drones. Mars has rocks that are fixed in place and react when things get close to them. The Outpost has objects that're part of the environment and also has its own status display on the screen.
Players check suit battery, solar intensity, storm intensity, power usage, power available and emergency status on a tablet. The game has functions that update these values in one place. When the screen is closed the Outpost goes back to the way it was before.
The project helps players understand the risks of a mission and the decisions, about resources through playing the game. It can help kids learn how environmental dangers, broken equipment and not enough supplies can affect the safety of the crew and the success of the mission.
details:
Week As A Marstronaut is a browser-based Mars exploration and survival game where players control a rover on the Martian surface and an astronaut inside a habitat. Players monitor survival statistics, explore the terrain and interact with different systems designed to simulate life on Mars.

The game makes the challenges of space survival easier and more engaging to understand, especially for young learners. Its simple pixel-art interface, interactive environments and browser-based design make it accessible without requiring specialised hardware.

AstroTrainer aims to educate students about the challenges of establishing human life on Mars, including resource management, radiation protection, power and food production. It makes these scientific and engineering concepts more interactive through gameplay.

We used JavaScript, JSX, CSS and HTML, with React 19 for the interface, Phaser 4 for game development and Vite 8 as the build tool. We also used Git and GitHub for version control, along with pixel-art assets for the game's characters and environments.

AstroTrainer combines two interconnected environments: a rover exploring Mars and an astronaut managing a habitat. Its pixel-art visuals, futuristic interface and planned NASA-data-based storm warning system bring space exploration and survival together in an interactive experience.

We focused on balancing scientific concepts with simple, engaging gameplay suitable for younger audiences. We also considered accessibility, clear visual indicators, resource management and a modular code structure that allows us to expand the game with new features.
